Seen on reading the planned edits before the cut, after the author's word on the grades; the cut made as banked and approved, the marks named here for the next re-cut's planner.

(b) THE SEAT'S: A RE-RUN THAT READ A CUT ONE-WORD ROW AS STANDING. The first re-run of the grade bank at the branch (tools/b657_record.py _regrade) looked for each graded sentence anywhere in its file and so read #31 s22 ("Clean.", the distinctFromInput row, cut) as OVERREACHES STANDING, the same word standing as the eulerConsuming row's MATCHES "Clean." in the same file. Caught at that first run, before the cut bank was committed; the re-run now reads a row as cut when its sentence occurs fewer times at the branch than at main, and the control at main reads every graded row standing (78).
